newsitem.title: ITALY: Spanish, Italian firms take stakes in San Paolo.
newsitem.headline: Spanish, Italian firms take stakes in San Paolo.

text.p: Banco Santander, Fiat holding IFI, Italian banks IMI and Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena, and Italian insurer Reale Mutua Assicurazioni will become core shareholders in San Paolo bank, which will be privatised later this year.

A statement from the Compagnia which indirectly controls Istituto Bancario San Paolo di Torino, said Santander, IFI and IMI will take five percent each and Paschi and Reale will take three percent each.
The statement said the Compagnia di San Paolo on Wednesday approved the two-phase privatisation plan for San Paolo bank.
The Compagnia wholly owns a holding company called Gruppo Bancario San Paolo which currently controls around 65 percent of the bank.

The privatisation plan includes the formation of the core shareholding group with around 20 percent of the bank's capital via a private placement and a global public offering of some 25 percent of the bank's capital.
The statement said the Compagnia will participate in the stable shareholding group with a stake equal to five percent.
The price of the core shareholding stakes will be set at a later date at a meeting of the board of the Gruppo Bancario.
